item.title: I Who have never known men
item.description: This book made me think of memories, and how they fade away if you do not constantly narrate or recall them. This then connects to a sense of identity, and it is only built by constantly telling about (or reflecting on) your life. Without telling it, either to another person, or internalizing it in text, you’re only left fragments or disparate sensory reminders, and no story. In the novel, the narrator lives in an eternal, flat present once all her companions die.
